chunks: Al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"There is no prayer after the dawn (fajr) prayer until the sun rises, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, the sun rises between the two horns of Satan and sets between the two horns of Satan.' And he said: 'There is no prayer after the afternoon (asr) prayer until the evening (maghrib) prayer is performed.'"

key_terms.قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَان: Two horns of Satan (idiomatic expression for the time of sunrise)
key_terms.لاَ صَلاَة: No prayer (prohibition of voluntary prayer during specific times)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific times when voluntary prayers are prohibited after the obligatory prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the specific periods of *karaahat* (disliked time) for *nafl* prayers, distinguishing between the post-dawn prohibition linked to the sun's rising between the 'horns of Satan' and the post-afternoon period extending until *maghrib*. Shia jurists interpret the 'horns of Satan' metaphorically as the times when the sun is in a state of transition, marking the optimal window for voluntary worship before the obligatory *maghrib* prayer commences.
